Number of comments by item

Source: R/comments.R
delphi_comment_counts.Rd

Counts, for each round and item, the comments received, the experts who wrote them and the share of the experts who rated the item, and the comments written by experts whose ratings lie outside the interquartile range.

Usage

delphi_comment_counts(x, round = NULL, indicator = NULL, type = 7)

Arguments

x

A delphi_data object with comments; see delphi_add_comments().

round

Optional round number(s) to keep. NULL keeps all rounds.

indicator

Optional indicator on which the position of the authors is assessed. By default, a comment counts as coming from outside the interquartile range when its author lies outside it on at least one indicator.

type

Quantile algorithm; see delphi_describe().

Value

A data frame of class delphi_comment_counts with one row per round and item, including the items without comments, and columns round, item, n_comments, n_experts (experts who commented), n_raters (experts who rated the item), share_experts (n_experts / n_raters) and n_outside (comments from experts outside the interquartile range). Only rounds with at least one comment are included; general comments are not counted.

Examples

r1 <- data.frame(expert = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
                 E1 = c(7, 8, 6, 2), E2 = c(3, 5, 4, 9))
x <- delphi_data(r1, expert_col = "expert", indicator = "impact")
cm <- data.frame(expert = c("A", "D", "D"), item = c("E1", "E1", "E2"),
                 comment = c("Depends on public funding.",
                             "Unlikely without new regulation.",
                             "The statement is too broad."))
x <- delphi_add_comments(x, cm)
delphi_comment_counts(x)
#>  round item n_comments n_experts n_raters share_experts n_outside
#>      1   E1          2         2        4          0.50         1
#>      1   E2          1         1        4          0.25         1
